$comment: ★ SPELLINGS BESIDE MSVC'S SIZED SUFFIXES THAT NO REFERENCE ACCEPTS. The C language document takes MSVC's 24 sized suffixes (`i8` … `ui64`, the `i` and the `u` each in either case; `integer_suffix_msvc_sized`) because MSVC accepts them; a spelling next to them is not thereby admitted — taking one would be an invention above `(gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C`. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-25 through `dssharness run probe-reference-cc`: MSVC 19.51.36260 (`/std:c17`) refuses each spelling here (C2059 'bad suffix on number'), and so do gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c11 -pedantic-errors` and the default mode) and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 ('invalid suffix') — a width MSVC has no type for (`5i128`, `5i7`), a leading zero (`5i08`), C23's character-prefix spelling (`5u8`), the `u` misplaced or doubled (`5iu64`, `5i64u`, `5uu64`), a second suffix after a sized one (`5ui64l`) or before it (`5LLi64`), and a doubled `i` (`5Ii64`). DSS reports each as its own P_MalformedNumber at its own position. The pin was written in P68 round 13 together with the change that admitted the 24, to hold the boundary that change must not cross. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: list `i128` in the language document (with a rule to cover it) and its diagnostic disappears, so the set no longer matches.
